en: The Megha Sūtra. Homage to all the perfectly awakened Buddhas, who are an inconceivable ocean.
Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling in the palace of the nāga kings Nanda and Upananda,
in the peaked pavilion of the great cloud-circle containing the glorious jewel-treasury, together with a great saṅgha of bhikṣus, a great saṅgha of bodhisattvas,
and a great assembly of nāgas, such as the nāga king Nanda, the nāga king Upananda, Sāgara, Anavatapta, Manasvin, Varuṇa, Takṣaka, Ghṛtarāṣṭra, and Vāsuki.
and by the nāga king Mucilinda— headed by these and preceded by all the nāga kings, eighty-four hundred thousand *koṭī-niyuta* of nāgas assembled and took their seats.
Then, at that time, all those nāga kings together with their retinues rose from their seats, draped their upper robes over one shoulder, and placed their right knees upon the ground.

Bowing with palms joined toward where the Blessed One was, they made offerings with immeasurable and incalculable varieties of most exquisite flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, silk streamers, musical instruments, cymbals, drums, and songs; with jeweled flowers, jeweled necklaces, pearl necklaces, *nāgapuṣpa* flowers, and nets of pearls; resounding, rattling, fanning great winds, and roaring a great roar while uttering delightful sounds of the Dharma, they completely covered the Blessed One with great reverence, veneration, and wonder.
They circumambulated him;
having circumambulated him, they stood to one side. Standing to one side, they made aspirational prayers.
With oceans of bodies as numerous as the atoms in all the oceans of world-systems, [he entered] into the oceans of the circles of assemblies of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
into the oceans of the expansions of all world-systems;
and into every single atom that is equal to the atoms of all earth, water, fire, and wind, and equal to the atoms of the manifestation of all forms—in each and every such atom.

With oceans of clouds of bodies that have transcended all calculation— being incalculable, immeasurable, inconceivable, incomparable, unfathomable, and beyond description— and having empowered within each single body immeasurable and incalculable oceans of clouds, facing the currents of all directions from every single atom-dust particle with unimpeded expansions reaching the shores of all directions, may we honor, revere, respect, and worship the oceans of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas with oceans of clouds of every kind of offering.

Namely, having presided over the expanse of space covered by immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable, incomparable, unobtainable, infinite, and indescribable, yet undifferentiated oceans and clouds of the power of Samantabhadra’s conduct—
just as it is with the oceans and clouds of the bodies of Bodhisattvas,
so too with the oceans and clouds of all the solar and lunar mandalas of bodies that are dense with rays of light of every precious color.
With clouds of oceans of all-jewel-necklace-flowers;
with clouds of oceans of gabled palaces containing the radiance of all jewels within;
with clouds of oceans of treasuries of all-powdered-incense trees.
With ocean-clouds of all fragrances, incenses, and manifestations of all forms;
with ocean-clouds of the thundering of all sounds and musical instruments;
and with ocean-clouds of all fragrant trees.
Abiding upon a completely covered expanse of the sky,
with these and other such immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable, incomparable, unmeasurable, infinite, ineffable, and undifferentiated oceans of clouds of all manner of offerings,
may we honor, revere, respect, and worship all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
(And so on for half a dozen pages, enumerating the various ornaments, each compounded with *samudrameghaiḥ* and constructed with the same four potencies.)
Having made such a vow, those nāga kings again circumambulated the Blessed One three times and paid homage at his feet.
Permitted by the Blessed One, they sat down upon their respective seats.
Now, at that time, there was Anantaparikarasāgarameghavyūhatejomaṇḍalacchatrākārarāja, the sovereign of the great nāgas of the triple-thousand great-thousandfold world system.

Rising from his seat, draping his upper robe over one shoulder, and placing his right knee upon the ground, he bowed with palms joined toward where the Blessed One was and addressed the Blessed One as follows:
"I would ask the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksambuddha, a certain question regarding a particular point,
if the Blessed One would grant me the opportunity to have my question answered."
When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the lord of nāgas, Anantaparikarasāgarameghavyūhatejomaṇḍalachatrākārarāja:
"Ask, O lord of serpents, whatever you desire; I shall satisfy your mind by answering each and every question.
When this had been said, the great lord of nāgas, Anantaparikarachatrākārarāja of the triple-thousand great-thousandfold world system, spoke thus to the Blessed One:
"How, Blessed One,
might all the nāgas have their sufferings completely stilled, become joyful, and be endowed with happiness; and how might they release showers of rain here in Jambudvīpa from time to time,
causing all grasses, shrubs, medicinal herbs, and forest trees to grow?"
May they cause all crops to grow and produce all flavors,
so that the humans of Jambudvīpa may be endowed with happiness.

When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to King Anantaparikara, the sovereign of the great nāgas of the triple-thousand world system: "Excellent, excellent, O Lord of Nāgas! It is well that you have set out for the welfare and happiness of all sentient beings, and that you consider it necessary to question the Tathāgata regarding this matter. Therefore, O Lord of Nāgas, listen and attend closely and well."
I shall speak to you,
O Lord of Serpents: by being endowed with a single quality, all the sufferings of all the nāgas would be stilled,
and they would become established in happiness.
By what single dharma? Namely, by loving-kindness (*maitrī*). In that regard, O Lord of Serpents, gods and humans who dwell in loving-kindness are not burned by fire.
They are not harmed by weapons; they are not carried away by water;
they are not killed by poison.
They are not overcome by foreign armies; they sleep in peace and awaken in peace, and they are protected by their own merit.

They are inflamed by the splendor of great merit; they become invincible to the world including the gods; they are gracious in appearance; they are pleasant to behold; they possess unimpeded movement everywhere; all their sufferings are stilled; they are filled with joy and endowed with every happiness.

And furthermore, O Lord of Serpents, after the dissolution of the body, those who have realized the superhuman state through their conduct will be reborn in the Brahma-world by means of friendly mental action.
These, O Lord of Serpents, are the benefits for gods and humans who dwell in friendliness.
Therefore, O Lord of Serpents, one should dwell with friendly bodily action, friendly verbal action, and friendly mental action.
Furthermore, Lord of Serpents, the dhāraṇī named Sarvasukhadadā should be set in motion.
It pacifies all the sufferings of the nāgas and bestows all forms of happiness;
by means of it, rain-showers are released from time to time here in Jambudvīpa.
It causes all grasses, shrubs, medicinal herbs, forest trees, and crops to grow.
In this regard, Lord of Nagas, what is that dhāraṇī called "Bestower of All Happiness"? It is as follows:
*dharaṇi dhāraṇi*.

The Deliverer, the Well-Established, the Victorious, the One of True Color and Truthful Promise, the One Possessing Natural Wisdom, the Producer, the Destroyer, the Consecrated, and the One Whose Utterance is Auspicious.
O Unborn One, O Great Mother!
O Carrier of the Vessel!
Remove my afflictions!
Shake off evil! Cleanse the paths!
Make the tracks smooth upon the dharmas.
Furthermore, Lord of Nagas,

you should retain in mind the names of those Tathāgatas who belong to the lineage and clan that has issued from the tip of a single hair of Vairocana, who possess the splendor of the array of the empowerment arising from the Meghakula, and whose wisdom-banner illuminates the realm of nirvāṇa like a moon-maṇḍala at night.
These should be brought to mind;

they pacify all the sufferings of all nāgas— of all nāga clans, all nāga lineages, all nāgas born from every source, all nāga wombs, all nāga kings, and all nāga maidens resplendent with clouds arising from all nāga families, as well as all the retinues of nāgas.
They provide all the requisites for happiness.
In this regard, O Lord of Nagas, what are those names of the Tathāgata?
They are as follows: Homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocanagarbha-mahāmegha.
Homage to the Blessed One, who is resplendent with clouds born from the lineage of the Nāgas.

O Lord of Serpents, by the recitation of these names of the Tathāgatas, all the sufferings of all the nāgas are completely stilled, and those who were afflicted by suffering release showers of rain here in Jambudvīpa from time to time, causing all grasses, shrubs, medicinal herbs, trees, and crops to grow.
Then indeed, Anantaparikara... the lord of the nāgas, entreated the Blessed One:

"May the Blessed One speak such dhāraṇī-mantra phrases by which, in this Jambudvīpa, during the final time, in the final age, when there is no rain, great torrents of rain may fall upon being uttered.

[May they be spoken] at the time of a terrible age, at the time of a wilderness age, at the time of unrighteous people, strife, and discord, at the time of calamities and afflictions, at the time of disease and death, and at the time of the unfavorable configuration of the planets."

May he, through the empowerment of the Buddha, effect the pacification of all calamities and afflictions. May the Blessed One, who is supremely compassionate and sympathetic toward all sentient beings, speak such dhāraṇī-mantra words as would incite all the nāgas.
They would cause all the gods to rejoice;
they would shatter all the Māras;

they would ward off all slaughter against all sentient beings, as well as their fears, calamities, and afflictions, and they would perform rites for peace and well-being; and they would pacify whatever is caused by unfavorable constellations.
May they all dispel whatever obstacles to rain have been spoken of by the Blessed One;
may they release proper showers of rain here in Jambudvīpa.
For this purpose, I entreat the Blessed Tathāgata.
When this had been said, the Blessed One, surrounded by an infinite retinue, spoke thus to the Lord of Nagas:
"Excellent, excellent, O Lord of Serpents, that you entreat the Tathāgata for the sake, welfare, and happiness of all sentient beings.
Therefore, O Lord of Serpents, listen and attend well and thoroughly; I shall speak to you."
The *Dhāraṇī* named *Mahākaruṇodbhava-mahāmegha-nirnnādavijṛmbhita-sūryaketu*, spoken by all the Buddhas, empowered and rejoiced in, for the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings:
it causes rain to fall during drought and restrains excessive rain.
It pacifies the wilderness of death;
it rouses all the nāgas;
and it gladdens all the gods.
It destroys all Māras and bestows all happiness upon all sentient beings. It is as follows:
*mahājñānāvabhāsani śrītejolakṣmīdṛḍhavikramavajrasaṃhanane paramavirajanirmalaguṇaketusūryaprabhe vimalāṅgayaṣṭi bhara bhara saṃbhara sara sara sire sire suru suru* for the Nāgas.
Java 2 jivi 2 juvu 2 mahānāgā āgacchata... O great nāgas, pour down rain upon Jambudvīpa!
O great nāgas, release showers of rain here in Jambudvīpa through the empowerment of the truth of all the gods... Svāhā!
Through the empowerment of the truth of Brahmā, let it rain here in Jambudvīpa! Svāhā!
By the truth of Śakra, may there be victory, svāhā! By the truth of the Four Great Kings, may there be victory... By the truth of the eightfold [path], may there be victory...
By the truth of the stream-enterer...
| by the truth of the once-returner... | by the truth of the non-returner...
By the truth of the Arhats... by the truth of the Pratyekabuddhas... Homage to all Buddhas! May the mantra words be effective, svāhā!
The sixty-fourth chapter, titled "The Arrival of the Rain from the Great Cloud of the Hundred Thousand [Verses] Mahāyāna Sūtra."

The ritual procedure for one desiring a great rain is as follows: on a clean and spacious plot of ground, under a blue canopy spread out in the open air with blue banners raised aloft, the Dharma-preacher, having fasted according to the eightfold precepts, with his body well-washed and wearing clean garments, shall sit upon a blue seat.

One who eats the three-fold sacrificial food (triśulka) and has been anointed with fragrant perfumes should revolve this Great Maṇḍala of the Clouds while facing the east, reciting it day and night without interruption.
Having invoked all the Tathāgatas, four full jars filled with clear blue water should be placed there, along with offerings of bali, incense, and flowers according to one's ability.

There, having drawn a lotus with cow-dung juice upon the ground in the four directions for the sake of the Dharma-preacher, one should draw the Naga King named Triśīrṣaka, surrounded by a retinue of Nagas, measuring three cubits in the eastern direction using cow-dung.

In the southern direction, a nāga king named Pañcaśīrṣaka, accompanied by a retinue of nāgas, should be depicted measuring five cubits. In the western direction, a nāga king named Saptaśīrṣaka, accompanied by a retinue of nāgas, should be depicted measuring seven cubits.
In the northern direction, [a nāga king] named Navaśīrṣaka, measuring nine cubits... [should be depicted].

The Dharma-preacher, having protected himself and dwelling in loving-kindness (*maitrī*) toward all sentient beings, should attend to them with a compassionate mind. Having invoked all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, he should share this ritual procedure with the *nāgas* by means of his own roots of merit.
Afterwards, during a time of drought, if he recites this chapter on the Great Cloud Mandala for one day, two days, or up to seven nights, it will certainly cause rain to fall.

Even the ocean might overstep its shore, but the auspicious utterance "the rain shall not fall" cannot be otherwise. However, it must certainly be recited by one endowed with moral discipline (*śīla*), virtuous qualities (*guṇa*), and so forth, while partaking of food such as milk-rice, molasses, and milk, or the "three sweets"— clarified butter, honey, and molasses— as Vādirāja himself has stated.
Homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya.
Homage to the Tathāgata Amitāyus. Homage to the Tathāgata Śākyamuni. ||0||

Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling upon the great ocean in a gabled chamber with a peak made of precious jewels, together with a great host of nāgas—comprising a full thousand nāgas—all of whom possessed great supernatural power, accompanied by a vast retinue of nāgas.
Namely: Nanda and...

Together with these and many thousands of other great nāga kings, all those nāga kings— possessed of great nāga-miraculous power and great nāga-transformations— came through the sky with a thundering roar, releasing great winds and rain,
in order to serve the Blessed One and to hear the Dharma.
At that time, the Blessed One gave his approval to the great nāgas.
Excellent, O two Nāgas! O great Nāgas!

Adorned with the arrays of the miraculous manifestations of great clouds, [the world-systems were] graced by great ocean-clouds of hanging necklaces of pearls, strings of jewels, and beautiful nets of golden filigree upon all their jewel-peaks... (here follow approximately twenty long compounds describing ornaments and so forth).
...each ending with "meghaiḥ" (with clouds)... may they completely cover the sky!
May all the nāga kings come to this circle of the earth, reign, rain, pour down rain, roar "huduhudu," display great lightning, and manifest themselves, clashing and colliding together.
Crackling and gurgling, emitting delightful and great sounds like the roars of mighty elephants, proclaiming a great resonance:
"Rain down upon Jambudvīpa, svāhā!
Come, come, O mighty elephants, svāhā!"
I invoke Pauṇḍra, the king of the nāgas, by the truth of the Buddha: rain down here in Jambudvīpa, svāhā!
I invoke Śrīteja, the king of the nāgas, by the truth of the Dharma: rain down here in Jambudvīpa, svāhā! Ananta, [by the truth] of the Saṅgha... [may there be] joy and peace.
Vāsuki, the nāga, is the *ja-pasa* of Vajrapāṇi;
Takṣaka is the *ja-pasa* of Brahmā;
Śrīkaṇṭha is the *ja-pasa* of Indra.
He is not Erāvaṇa, O Viṣṇu;
he is not Śiva, O Satya;
he is not a high-minded sage, O Ṛṣi.
By truth, he causes all nāgas to flee; by truth, he causes the yakṣas to tremble; by truth, he causes the rākṣasas to be terrified at Lake Anavatapta.
All you nāgas, rain down, rain down by means of truth!
Do not delay; come, O great nāgas! I urge on all the nāga-lakes. I summon you:
*sara* 2, *hara* 2, *dhapa* 2, *hāhāhāhā hi* 4... *ehehi tha* 3, *cacacacarata*! Fill all the fields and rain down all kinds of crops; release great winds!
Druṃ 2 ghri 2 pṛṃ 2 ṭā 4 ṇi cāriṇi! O you who paralyze and delude! O Jāṅgulī, Pukkaśī, Brahmāṇī, Mātaṅgī, Jayā, Vijayā, svāhā!
I impel all the great thundering clouds for the sake of the Tathāgata Mahāmegha-śrī-tejas.
To the Tathāgata Mahāmeghasphoṭaka!
By the empowerment of all Buddhas, by the empowerment of all Bodhisattvas, and by the truth of all Nāgas, I invoke the hearts of all Nāgas: come quickly! By the consent of the Three Jewels;
homage to the Three Jewels!
Homage to Caṇḍavajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣas, O you of beautiful form who binds and binds, you whose form is Time, svāhā!
Having previously performed the protective rite, the reciter of the Dharma should tie a knot with a corner of his robe after it has been empowered by seven recitations.
This "Revolution of the Circle of Winds," known as the Heart of All Nāgas, should be recited.
Without interruption for three weeks,
one should draw in the eastern direction the Naga King named Triśīrṣa with his retinue using cow dung;
in the southern direction, one should draw the serpent named Pañcaśīrṣa Prasphoṭana.

In the western direction, the Naga king named Avabhāsanaśikhī, with seven heads, should be depicted together with his retinue of Nagas. To the north, the Naga king named Meghasañcodana, with nine heads, should be painted.

A blue canopy, blue garments, and a blue banner should be provided, and the entire offering for the Nagas should be blue; however, a sweet offering should be made for the Nagas, and the three sweets (trimadhura) should be offered as all the oblations (āhuti) with the Heart-mantra of the Nagas.
And the kings of clouds are to be painted as they release showers of rain; they should be depicted clashing against one another,
and at the edge, garlands of lightning and *cakora* birds are to be drawn.
A svastika, a canopy, parched grain, fish, meat, honey, and edible fruits should be offered;
furthermore, a generous sacrificial offering (bali) must be made here.
Then, the Dharma-preacher, being pure and dressed in clean garments, should recite the *Nāgahṛdaya* while turning the wind-circle (*vātamaṇḍali*).
Then, beginning from the first day, the nāgas make a gulugula sound;
they utter delightful sounds, and there is neither failure nor contradiction of the command regarding this cycle.
If the ocean were to overstep its shore, then this rain would likewise overstep its bounds.
Homage to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksambuddha Śrīīgarbhakūṭavinarditarāja!
Homage to the Blessed One! May there be well-being for me; may there be loving-kindness for all sentient beings;
may there be fearlessness toward all living creatures.
May all the miserable destinies of those who have gone as animals be pacified. Homage to Sarvanivāraṇaviṣkambhin!
May this rite of all the Tathāgatas be accomplished!
The ritual procedure for being beheld by all the Buddhas is as follows:
*Sphaṭa* seven times, *svāhā*.
Whoever it may be who has bathed their head—
whether a monk, a nun,
or a lay follower.
Or a female lay follower, dressed in clean garments and with a mind of loving-kindness,
having written down these names of the Tathāgatas and placed them on a pure seat, should lift seven incense burners into the air and recite the names of the Tathāgatas five times for each.
Having performed a great worship, during a drought, it should be recited continuously for seven days;
then the rain-god will send down rain.
Thus ends the sixty-fifth chapter, the "Vātamaṇḍalī-parivarta," from the *Śrīmahāmegha*, a Mahāyāna Sūtra.
